redFirst.basis: regression mode, expectRedFirst false; the defect reproduces only on windows-latest

outcome.technical: Cause (reasoned from the CI line plus code, not run on Windows): submit_command built the in-tree manifest with os.path.join(project, 'docs/audit/audit-plan.json'). The plan records the manifest with '/'; on Windows os.path.join keeps it, giving 'C:\\p\\docs/audit/audit-plan.json' (mixed separators), while the case expected os.path.join of separate parts (all backslashes), so the substring did not match. The writer held the defect (mixed-separator path printed in an agent-run command), not the case. Fix: new absolute_manifest(project, manifest, path=os.path) = path.normpath(path.join(...)) in audit-lookup.py, used by submit_command. Assumption and source: ntpath.join does not rewrite '/' in a later component and ntpath.normpath converts '/' to '\\' (Python docs for os.path.normpath: 'On Windows, it converts forward slashes to backward slashes'). Pinned on every OS: new case bf44 calls absolute_manifest with ntpath and posixpath explicitly. Selftest 86/86 on macOS; ruff clean. Orchestrator's next windows CI run verifies bf42.
outcome.descriptive: A wave task's submit block now prints the phase tree's manifest in one separator style on Windows.

testsAdded: plugins/audit/tests/test_audit_lookup.py: bf44 (ntpath/posixpath shape of absolute_manifest); bf42 expected to pass on windows-latest
claims: claims: absolute_manifest docstring states only the separator behaviour (ntpath join/normpath), basis the Python docs; bf44 pins it with ntpath on all OSes, so it does not depend on the host.
